title: 第七章 柢山之难第八章 看丘幻影
lines: 第七章：柢山之难
下潜的计划最终被放弃了。
不是因为技术不可行，也不是因为恐惧，而是因为那条赤鳕。
在陈宇消失后的第三天，那头原本在深潭中翻滚哀嚎的巨兽，突然以一种违背物理常识的姿态，垂直沉入了潭底最深的淤泥之中。它的下沉过程极其诡异，庞大的身躯没有激起一丝涟漪，就像一滴墨水滴入宣纸，悄无声息地融入了那片永恒的黑暗。
紧接着，整个赤水潭的水位开始以肉眼可见的速度下降。
“虹吸现象？”黄海涛趴在岩壁上，看着水位线每天下降半米，露出一圈圈被强酸腐蚀得坑坑洼洼的黑色岩壁。
“不，是地下暗河改道了。”李元茜用一根长藤蔓吊着，深入到潭边的一个排水口处，那里原本是汹涌的出水口，现在已经变成了进气口，正发出呜呜的怪响，“这下面的地质结构不稳定。赤鳕的死亡或者某种信号，触发了地壳的连锁反应。”
她话音刚落，脚下的大地传来一阵沉闷的轰鸣。
不是地震那种剧烈的摇晃，而是一种更深沉、更压抑的震动，像是巨兽在肠胃里翻滚。
“走！”黄海涛大吼一声，一把拽住李元茜，两人刚脱离藤蔓，身后的岩壁便轰然崩塌。数十吨重的玄武岩像积木一样垮塌，激起漫天的红色泥浆。那个深不见底的赤水潭，在短短几分钟内，被彻底填平，变成了一个巨大的、冒着硫磺蒸汽的泥坑。
迷榖树指引的终点，陈宇消失的地方，就这样被大自然亲手封印了。
“现在怎么办？”李元茜坐在地上，满脸的泥污，眼神中却透着不甘。
黄海涛抹了一把脸上的汗，看着那个被封死的泥坑，又抬头望向迷榖树的方向。那棵巨树的光芒依旧温柔，但它投射出的光影地图，在赤鳕消失后，已经变得残缺不全。
“路断了。”黄海涛沉声道，“但《南山经》的路标没断。‘又东三百里，曰柢山。’”
他摊开李元茜绘制的那张残缺地图，指向迷榖树光影消散前最后闪烁的一个标记点。那个点位于赤水潭的东南方，标注着一座山的简笔画，山下画着一条弯曲的河流，旁边写着两个字：柢山。
“柢山……‘有鱼焉，其状如牛，陵居，蛇尾，有翼，其羽在下，其音如留牛，其名曰鲑。其鸣自訆，见则天下大旱。’”黄海涛背诵着经文，“这描述……听起来不像鱼，倒像是一种能在陆地上生活的两栖巨兽。”
“鲑？见则天下大旱？”李元茜皱眉，“这矛盾了。鱼需要水，大旱又意味着缺水。除非……它是一种能调节水分的生物？”
两人收拾起残存的装备，放弃了那个被封印的泥坑，转而向着迷榖树最后指引的东南方进发。
离开赤水盆地后，地貌再次发生剧变。火山岩消失，取而代之的是一种松软的、灰白色的粉砂岩。植被变得稀疏而怪异，到处都是长着巨大球状根茎的植物，像一个个倒扣的碗，半埋在沙土里。
气温急剧升高。空气干燥得像要把人榨干，每一次呼吸都带着灼痛感。这里的天空呈现出一种病态的淡黄色，太阳不再是一个圆盘，而是一团模糊的、散发着白色光晕的炽热球体。
“这是……沙漠化前兆？”黄海涛看着便携式温湿度计，读数已经爆表，“相对湿度低于10%，地表温度超过60摄氏度。这绝不是正常的气候带。”
“看那边！”李元茜指着远方地平线上的一道黑线。
那是一道巨大的、正在移动的沙墙。它不像普通的沙尘暴那样混沌，而是呈现出一种诡异的规律性，像一条蜿蜒的黑色巨蟒，贴着地面快速向他们的方向移动。
“跑！”黄海涛只来得及喊出这一个字。
两人转身就跑，但那沙墙的速度太快了。眨眼间，黑色的沙粒就像潮水一样淹没了他们的脚踝，然后是大腿，最后是腰部。
但这沙子很奇怪。它们并不粗糙，反而带着一种油腻的光泽，而且温度极低，贴在皮肤上像冰块一样。更诡异的是，那些沙粒仿佛有生命一般，顺着裤管向上攀爬，疯狂地钻进他们的衣服里。
“这不是沙！是虫！”李元茜惊恐地拍打身上的黑色颗粒。
借着微弱的阳光，两人看清了。那根本不是沙子，而是无数只体长只有几毫米的、长着六条腿的黑色甲虫。它们密密麻麻地聚集在一起，像一条流动的黑色河流，所过之处，地面上的一切绿色植物都在瞬间枯萎、碳化，仿佛被抽干了所有水分。
“柢山之难……”黄海涛想起《山海经》里的记载，心中一片冰凉，“古籍里说的‘见则天下大旱’，指的就是这种东西！”
那些黑甲虫并没有立刻攻击他们。它们像潮水一样从两人身边流过，向着迷榖树的方向涌去。在那黑色的虫潮中心，一个巨大的、由无数甲虫背负着的平台，正缓缓移动着。
平台上，坐着一个身影。
是那个红发女人。
她依旧赤足，稳稳地站在那不断蠕动的虫群平台上，仿佛脚下不是数以亿计的甲虫，而是一块坚固的浮冰。她手中的发光权杖此刻正向下指着，杖尖射出一道淡蓝色的光柱，精准地控制着虫潮的流向。
而在她的身边，跪着几个灰白色的身影。
是那些“黑齿国”的土著。但此刻，他们看起来已经不成人形。皮肤干瘪得像风干的橘子皮，眼窝深陷，嘴唇干裂出血。他们手里捧着简陋的陶罐，正在接取从虫潮中滴落的一种粘稠的、散发着清香的液体。
“那是……水？”黄海涛瞪大了眼睛。
“不是水，是汁液。”李元茜的声音在颤抖，“这些甲虫在分泌一种高浓度的保湿液！它们在掠夺植物的水分，然后集中起来！那个红发女人在收集它们！”
就在这时，红发女人似乎感应到了什么，缓缓转过头。她的目光穿透了黑色的虫潮，落在了躲在岩石缝隙里的两人身上。
她的眼神中没有杀意，只有一种极度的疲惫和……警告。
她抬起权杖，不再是攻击，而是轻轻一挥。一道淡蓝色的光幕瞬间展开，挡在了她和虫潮与两人之间，将外界的灼热和虫群的躁动隔绝在外。

Chapter 7: Disaster at Mount Zhe
1.
The dive plan was eventually abandoned.
Not because the technology wasn't feasible, or because of fear, but because of the red cod.
On the third day after Chen Yu disappeared, the giant beast that was rolling and wailing in the deep pool suddenly sank vertically into the deepest mud at the bottom of the pool in an attitude that defied common sense of physics. Its sinking process is extremely strange. Its huge body does not cause a single ripple, just like a drop of ink dripping into rice paper, quietly blending into the eternal darkness.
Immediately afterwards, the water level in the entire Chishuitan began to drop at a speed visible to the naked eye.
"Siphon phenomenon?" Huang Haitao lay on the rock wall and watched the water level drop by half a meter every day, revealing circles of black rock walls that were corroded by strong acid.
"No, the underground river has changed its course." Li Yuanqian was hung by a long vine and went deep into a drainage outlet beside the pool. It was originally a turbulent water outlet, but now it has become an air inlet and is making a strange whine. "The geological structure below is unstable. The death of red cod or some kind of signal triggered a chain reaction in the earth's crust."
As soon as she finished speaking, there was a dull roar from the ground beneath her feet.
It was not the violent shaking of an earthquake, but a deeper and more depressing vibration, like a giant beast rolling in the stomach.
"Let's go!" Huang Haitao yelled and grabbed Li Yuanqian. As soon as the two of them got away from the vines, the rock wall behind them suddenly collapsed. Dozens of tons of basalt collapsed like building blocks, stirring up red mud that filled the sky. The bottomless Chishui Pond was completely filled up in just a few minutes and turned into a huge mud pit with sulfur steam rising out of it.
The end point guided by the myrtle tree, the place where Chen Yu disappeared, was sealed by nature.
"What should we do now?" Li Yuanqian sat on the ground, her face covered in mud, but her eyes showed unwillingness.
Huang Haitao wiped the sweat from his face, looked at the sealed mud pit, and then looked up in the direction of the mist tree. The light of the giant tree is still gentle, but the light and shadow map it projects has become incomplete after the disappearance of Red Cod.
"The road is broken." Huang Haitao said solemnly, "But the road sign in "Nanshan Sutra" is not broken. 'Three hundred miles to the east, it is called Mount Zhe.'"
He unfolded the incomplete map drawn by Li Yuanqian and pointed to the last flickering mark before the light and shadow of the mist tree disappeared. That point is located in the southeast of Chishuitan. It is marked with a simple drawing of a mountain. A curved river is drawn at the foot of the mountain, and two words are written next to it: 梢山.
"Zheshan...'There is a fish. Its shape is like an ox, with a mausoleum, a snake tail, wings, its feathers are down, and its sound is like an ox. Its name is salmon. Its cry is self-proclaimed, and when you see it, there will be a severe drought in the world.'" Huang Haitao recited the scripture, "This description... doesn't sound like a fish, but like an amphibious giant beast that can live on land."
"Salmon? Will there be a severe drought in the world?" Li Yuanqian frowned, "This is a contradiction. Fish need water, and a severe drought means lack of water. Unless... it is a creature that can regulate water?"
The two of them packed up the remaining equipment, abandoned the sealed mud pit, and headed to the southeast where the beacon tree finally guided them.
After leaving Chishui Basin, the landscape changed dramatically again. The volcanic rock disappeared and was replaced by a soft, off-white siltstone. The vegetation became sparse and weird, and there were plants with huge bulbous rhizomes everywhere, like upside-down bowls, half-buried in the sand.
The temperature rises sharply. The air was so dry that it felt like it was squeezing you dry, and every breath you took was burning. The sky here took on a sickly yellowish hue, and the sun was no longer a disk but a vague, fiery sphere with a white halo.
"Is this... a precursor to desertification?" Huang Haitao looked at the portable thermometer and hygrometer, and the readings were already off the charts. "The relative humidity is below 10%, and the surface temperature exceeds 60 degrees Celsius. This is by no means a normal climate zone."
"Look over there!" Li Yuanqian pointed to a black line on the horizon in the distance.
It was a huge, moving wall of sand. It was not as chaotic as ordinary sandstorms, but showed a strange regularity, like a winding black python, moving quickly in their direction close to the ground.
"Run!" Huang Haitao only had time to shout out this word.
The two turned around and ran, but the sand wall was too fast. In the blink of an eye, the black sand covered their ankles, then their thighs, and finally their waists like a tide.
But this sand is weird. They are not rough, but have a greasy sheen, and are extremely cold, sticking to the skin like ice cubes. What’s even weirder is that the sand particles seem to be alive, climbing up their pants legs and getting into their clothes crazily.
"This isn't sand! It's a bug!" Li Yuanqian slapped the black particles on her body in horror.
With the faint sunlight, the two of them could see clearly. It was not sand at all, but countless black beetles with six legs and a body length of only a few millimeters. They were densely packed together, like a flowing black river. Wherever it passed, all the green plants on the ground withered and carbonized in an instant, as if all the water had been drained.
"The disaster on Mount Zhe..." Huang Haitao thought of the records in "The Classic of Mountains and Seas", and his heart became cold. "The saying in ancient books, 'When you see it, there will be a severe drought in the world,' refers to this kind of thing!"
The black beetles did not attack them immediately. They flowed past the two of them like a tide, rushing in the direction of the banana tree. In the center of the black insect tide, a huge platform, carried by countless beetles, was moving slowly.
On the platform, a figure sat.
It's the red-haired woman.
She was still barefoot, standing steadily on the platform of the constantly wriggling insect swarm, as if her feet were not billions of beetles, but a solid ice floe. The luminous staff in her hand was pointing downward at the moment, and a light blue beam of light shot out from the tip of the staff, accurately controlling the flow of the insect tide.
Beside her, several gray-white figures were kneeling.
They are the natives of the "Black Tooth Country". But at this moment, they no longer looked human. The skin was as shriveled as dried orange peel, the eye sockets were sunken, and the lips were chapped and bleeding. They were holding simple clay pots in their hands, collecting a viscous, fragrant liquid dripping from the insect tide.
"That's...water?" Huang Haitao's eyes widened.
"It's not water, it's juice." Li Yuanqian's voice was trembling. "These beetles are secreting a high-concentration moisturizing fluid! They are robbing the plants of water and then concentrating it! The red-haired woman is collecting them!"
At this moment, the red-haired woman seemed to sense something and slowly turned her head. Her eyes penetrated the black insect tide and landed on the two people hiding in the crevices of the rocks.
There was no killing intent in her eyes, only a look of extreme exhaustion and... warning.
She raised her scepter, no longer attacking, but swiping lightly. A light blue light curtain instantly unfolded, blocking the space between her and the insect swarm, blocking out the scorching heat of the outside world and the restlessness of the insect swarm.
